observations: One 200 g water load at 100 g per step required two steps.
Double-load mode was tested, then base water raised to 500 g; effective water 1,000 g required ten steps.
Screenshot showed a cloth and evaporation arrows but no depicted water inventory or duration sequence.
Reveal states the fixed-rate doubling relationship and warns real drying rates change over time; slider label 500 g differs from effective 1,000 g in double mode.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish retained water from removal rate.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Two modes and a base-water slider.

whyCool: Changing how much water remains and changing how fast it leaves are different ways to affect drying.
caveat: No measured drying-time prediction; weak visual encoding and ambiguous base-water labeling.
effort: Prediction, both modes, maximum base water, screenshot and reveal.
bucketReason: Correct scoped arithmetic but weak visual explanation and cued prediction.

prediction.reason: The answer follows immediately from the stated fixed rate.
prediction.evidence: Which needs more steps: one load or double load.

interaction.reason: Base amount and doubled mode expose proportional duration.
interaction.evidence: 200 g takes two; effective 1,000 g takes ten.

payoff.reason: Explains the equation and limits of constant-rate drying.
payoff.evidence: Water amount and removal rate address different parts of the relationship.

clarity.reason: Base and effective amounts could be labeled more explicitly.
clarity.evidence: Water slider 500 g while Water readout says 1,000 g.

transfer.reason: Concrete distinction between spreading cloth and reducing retained water.
transfer.evidence: Different interventions affect different parts of the equation; actual rate varies.

surprise.evidence: More water at fixed rate requires more steps.

visualExplanation.reason: Cloth icon does not explain quantity or time.
visualExplanation.evidence: Evaporation arrows without a water or duration representation.

playfulness.evidence: Both modes and maximum water tested.

practicalValue.reason: Useful drying distinction with limited quantitative applicability.

depth.evidence: Real drying need not remain constant.
